## Body

F238 / PR #292 — deployed performance and transition-bounce receipt.

Before/after windows were recorded with the same observer. PID, kernel start seconds/microseconds and stamped commit stayed constant within each window. CPU is cumulative CPU-TIME slope, not snapshot %CPU; spawn subtraction is only within each incarnation. No old/new cumulative counter subtraction.

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon PID | 68755 | 9783 |
| Stamped commit | 0744555dee | 288d0d078f |
| Kernel start UTC | 2026-11-20 11:14:25.531067 | 2026-11-20 13:46:41.367437 |
| Window UTC | 13:42:20.527978–13:43:20.562384 | 13:48:41.413998–13:49:41.454765 |
| CPU-TIME observation interval | 60.030 s | 60.045 s |

| RSS, three readings (KiB) | 135136 / 135376 / 134128 | 198912 / 200304 / 157792 |

| Spawn delta / per-op deltas | 0 / all 0 | 0 / all 0 |
| Machine PID-counter births/s, separate 20 s sample | 35.320 | 29.485 |

The after window began 120 s after the new kernel start. That is an elapsed settling allowance, not proof of RSS equilibrium: after RSS fell substantially within this one window and remained higher than before. CPU differed by about +0.313 percentage points. Fleet/test work was uncontrolled; neither that CPU difference nor the global birth-rate decrease establishes causal cost or savings from F238. No presentation-improving rerun was taken.

No recorded daemon launch occurred during either 60 s window. This is observed quiet-window behavior, not proof that reconnect bursts or future control-client exits launch nothing. The after identity probe at 13:48:08 had 637 recorded spawns already; startup/reconnect work is outside the window. One leave thread per healthy exit, up to two new helper threads per pathological stuck exit, in-process reap polling and exit-only bounce sleeps remain the static costs in verdict 04240cd5921e8ec95dc5e3d1b2b4ecd3d01ec869.

Prime-owned transition, relayed by pm-001; UTC timestamps at second resolution:
- Pre-build 13:43:33–13:44:53: 80 s, separate from the bounce recipe.
- destroy-unattached switched off and bounce recipe began 13:44:53.
- bounce-rs rebuilt again: reported 76 s.
- SIGINT sent about 13:46:10. Old PID 68755 did not stop in its 30 s grace and required SIGKILL.
- New kernel start, independently observed: 13:46:41.367437; prime reported ready by 13:46:43.
- Bounce-start-to-ready envelope: 110 s, including the recipe build. Signal-to-ready envelope: approximately 33 s. Neither envelope is a measured socket/reconnect-unavailability interval; exact old-gone timing was not supplied.

Was the bounce slower? This transition used the full new 30 s graceful wait instead of the former recipe's fixed 0.5 s stop sleep. That is a longer observed wait than the old nominal sleep, not an empirical before/after end-to-end bounce benchmark: no prior comparable measured bounce duration was supplied. The two build intervals must not be charged as downtime. The timeout was on the old pre-F238 daemon, not a test of the new daemon's future Live::drop bound. SIGKILL means no graceful old-daemon teardown; prime reports the option was already off and the kill was harmless. Performance neither reran that reported failure nor bounced the new daemon to test it.

Observer/privacy boundary: canonical spawn-rate.py reads process argv and busy-polls, outside this seat's read-only privacy scope. Both windows instead use its same headline two-PID-counter method with /usr/bin/true edges, without argv inspection, parent attribution or the spin loop. PID wrapping uses the canonical convention; PID reuse/skips and the probe's own end edge qualify the headline estimate. No credential, prompt, token, environment, argv, message-body or transport-log inspection. CPU uses absolute /bin/ps; kernel start identity uses proc_pidinfo in-process. No performance-seat build, test, deployment, bounce or kill.
